summary: Aermotor LL-25 fire tower on Wakely Mountain in the Adirondacks, built 1916, closed for footing repairs in 2016-2018 and reopened to summit hikers.

facts.design: Aermotor LL-25 windmill-type tower with a 6 by 6 foot cab

access.note: State says it reopened after 2018 repairs. No later closure notice found in the sources read; check the state before visiting.

visit.trail_note: Hike to the summit in the Wakely Mountain Primitive Area; the state says visitors can climb the tower

events.note: Wooden fire tower that the 1916 tower replaced, per DEC
Aermotor LL-25; DEC says constructed 1916, replacing the 1911 wooden tower
New cabin for the observer's living quarters, per Conservation Commission report
64-foot outside ladder replaced by a factory stairway kit
Warren Meeker, forest ranger and fire observer, died while driving to the hamlet for supplies
International Paper and Finch, Pruyn donated a 1,200-acre tract that included the tower site
Last year of staffed fire observation
Placed on the National Register, per NHLR
Closed in December 2016 for footing deterioration, per NHLR; DEC dates the damage to winter 2017
June 2018 restoration; NHLR says all 8 footings were repaired, DEC says four were replaced

evidence.supports: Aermotor LL-25 with a 6 by 6 foot cab, one of the first built in the state in 1916
evidence.quote: The Aermotor LL-25 structure has a smaller 6’ x 6’ cab and was one of the first built in the state in 1916.

evidence.supports: constructed 1916, replacing a wooden tower built in 1911
evidence.quote: The fire tower was constructed in 1916, replacing a wooden fire tower constructed in 1911.

evidence.supports: 64-foot outside ladder replaced by a stairway kit in 1930
evidence.quote: originally had a 64-foot outside ladder which was replaced with a safer factory stairway kit in 1930.

evidence.supports: new observer's cabin in 1922
evidence.quote: 1922: A new cabin for the observer's living quarters was constructed.

evidence.supports: staffed and used for fire observation until 1988
evidence.quote: The fire tower was staffed and used for fire observation until 1988.

evidence.supports: not staffed since 1988, as of the 2016 visit report
evidence.quote: This tower has not been staffed since 1988.

evidence.supports: 1955 death of forest ranger and fire observer while driving for provisions
evidence.quote: Warren Meeker, a forest ranger and fire observer at Wakely Mountain, suffered a fatal heart attack yesterday while driving to this Adirondack hamlet for provisions.

evidence.supports: 1960 donation of a 1,200-acre tract to the people of New York
evidence.quote: A 1,200 acre tract of scenic Adirondack timberland was donated as a recreational area to the people of New York State by International Paper Company and Finch, Pruyn and Company, Inc.

evidence.supports: tower site was among the property donated, previously provided by the companies
evidence.quote: The property includes the site of the Wakeley Mountain fire tower previously provided by the companies for the protection of the Adirondack forests.

evidence.supports: 2001 field data gathered so the tower could be nominated to the National Register
evidence.quote: In 2001 Ann Spaziano–Mac Bride and Bill Starr completed field data gathering of this facility so that Indian Lake Town Historian Bill Zullo could nominate the station to the National Register of Historic Places.

evidence.supports: placed on the National Register in 2003
evidence.quote: The Wakely Mtn. station was placed on the National Register in 2003.

evidence.supports: registered March 6, 1995
evidence.quote:
Date Registered
March 6, 1995

evidence.supports: listed on the New York State and National Registers
evidence.quote: The AerMotor Model # LL‐25 tower is listed on the New York State and National Registers of Historic Places.

evidence.supports: footings were not fine in the October 2016 visit
evidence.quote: However, the footings are not fine.

evidence.supports: closed in December 2016 due to footing deterioration
evidence.quote: Due to footing deterioration, in December 2016, the NYSDEC closed the fire tower.

evidence.supports: wind damage in winter 2017 and the trail closed too
evidence.quote: The fire tower was damaged by winds during the winter of 2017, making it unsafe and in danger of toppling over. DEC closed the fire tower and the trail up the mountain for public safety reasons until repairs could be completed.

evidence.supports: June 2018 restoration, all 8 footings repaired
evidence.quote: In June 2018, the NYSDEC undertook a significant restoration of the Wakely Mountain fire tower, repairing all 8 footings, placing a new roof and new safety wire.

evidence.supports: eight days on the summit, four concrete footings replaced
evidence.quote: spent eight days on the mountain summit replacing all four concrete footings and installing new hardware and fasteners

evidence.supports: public can again hike to the summit, climb the tower, views of the central Adirondacks
evidence.quote: The public can once again hike to the summit of the mountain, climb the fire tower, and enjoy the 360° panoramic views of the central Adirondacks from the cab of the tower.

evidence.supports: tower sits in the Wakely Mountain Primitive Area
evidence.quote: Located in the Wakely Mountain Primitive Area

evidence.supports: tower in Hamilton County
evidence.quote: Hamilton County, New York

evidence.supports: radio repeater equipment and solar panels are in place
evidence.quote: Radio repeater equipment and solar panels are in place.

evidence.supports: NYS repeater inside the cab with its antenna on the south side; solar panel for power
evidence.quote: A NYS Repeater is installed inside the cab and its antenna is installed on the south side of the cab along with a solar panel for power generation.

evidence.supports: a visitor report from 2022
evidence.quote: Visited tower for 9th annual lighting.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the state use 'Wakely'; the Forest Lookouts page and the newspaper quotes it reproduces use 'Wakeley' for the same tower.

sources.title: Fire Tower and Trail to Mountain Summit Now Again Open to Public
sources.publisher: Adirondack Explorer (reprinting a NYS DEC announcement)

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on the closure cause and date (NHLR: footing deterioration, December 2016; DEC: wind damage in winter 2017) and on the number of footings (NHLR: 8 repaired in June 2018; DEC: 4 replaced). Height is 72 ft per NHLR and 70 ft per DEC, so height_m is left out. The DEC release is undated in the cached copy; its reopening is placed by the June 2018 NHLR entry. No closure notice after 2018 was found; the newest visitor report read is from 2022. Current access should be checked before publication. The 1955 newspaper and 1960 donation facts come from the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes newspapers without links. The DEC announcement is undated in the cache, so the story reports it as the state's announcement rather than as current status.
